numerical-ability.question: The prime numbers dividing 143 and leaving a remainder of 3 in each case are
numerical-ability.explanation:

Now, 140 = 5 × 7 × 4.
Hence, the required prime numbers are 5 and 7.

numerical-ability.question: The remainder obtained when any prime number greater than 6 is divided by 6 must be
numerical-ability.explanation:
Let the required prime number be p. Let p when divided by 6 give n as quotient and r as remainder.
 Then p = 6n + r, where 0 ≤ r < 6
Now, r = 0, r = 2, r = 3 and r = 4 do not give p as prime.
\textbackslash \ r ≠ 0, r ≠ 2, r ≠ 3 and r ≠ 4.
Hence, r = 1 or r = 5

numerical-ability.question: A pendulum strikes 5 times in 3 seconds and another pendulum strikes 7 times in 4 seconds. \nIf both pendulums start striking at the same time, how many clear strikes can be listened in 1 minute?
numerical-ability.explanation: \begin{array}{l}First\ pendulum\ strikes\ once\ in\ \frac{3}{5} seconds.\ Secondpendulum\ strikes\ once\ in\ \frac{4}{7} seconds.\\ \nL.C.M.\ of\ \ \frac{3}{5} \ and\frac{4}{7} =\ \frac{L.C.M.\ of\ \ \frac{3}{5}}{L.C.M.\ of\ \ \frac{4}{7}} =12\ So,\ they\ strike\ together\ after\ every\ 12\ seconds\\ \n\ .Thus,\ they\ strike\ together\left(\frac{60}{12} +1\right) =\ 6\ times\ in\ 1\ minute.\backslash \\ \ Total\ number\ of\ clear\ strikes\ heard=\left[\frac{60}{\left(\frac{3}{5}\right)} +\frac{60}{\left(\frac{4}{7}\right)}\right] -6=\left( 60*\frac{5}{3} +60*\frac{7}{4}\right) \ -6 =\ ( 100\ +\ 105) \ –\ 6\ =\ 199.\end{array}

numerical-ability.question:
The sum of the three consecutive even numbers is 44 more than the average of these numbers.
Which of the following is the third largest of these numbers?
numerical-ability.explanation: \begin{array}{l}Let\ the\ numbers\ be\ x,\ x\ +\ 2\ and\ x\ +\ 4.Then,( x\ +\ x\ +\ 2\ +\ x\ +\ 4) \ –\ \frac{\ ( x\ +\ x\ +\ 2\ +\ x\ +\ 4)}{3} =44\\ \Longrightarrow ( 3x+6) \ -\frac{( 3x+6)}{3} \ \ =44\\ \Longrightarrow 2( 3x+6) =132\Longrightarrow 6x=120\\ \Longrightarrow x=20 \end{array}

numerical-ability.question: Ratio between the ages of Subhash, Prasad and Amar is 3 : 6 : 7. If the difference between the ages of Prasad and Amar is 10 years, then what is the difference between the ages of Subhash and Prasad?
numerical-ability.explanation:
Let Subhash’s age be 3x years.
 Then, Prasad’s age = 6x years and Amar’s age = 7x years.
∴ 7x – 6x = 10 
⇒ x = 10. 
 Required difference = (6x – 3x) years = 3x years = (3 × 10) years = 30 years

numerical-ability.question: 3 men or 6 women can do a piece of work in 20 days. In how many days will 12 men and 8 women do the same work?
numerical-ability.explanation: \begin{array}{l}Let\ the\ required\ number\ of\ days\ be\ x.3\ men\ \equiv \ 6\ women\ \Leftrightarrow \ 12\ men\ \equiv \ ( 2\ \times \ 12)\ \ women=\ 24\ women.\backslash \ ( 12\ men\ and\ 8\ women) \ \equiv \ ( 24\ +\ 8)\\\ women\ =\ 32\ women.Now,\ More\ women,\ Less\ days\  \backslash \ 32\ :\ 6\ :\ :\ 20\ :\ x\ \Leftrightarrow \ 32x\ =\ 6\ \times \ 20\Leftrightarrow \ x\ =\left(\frac{6\ *20\ }{32}\right) =\frac{15}{4} =3\frac{3}{4}\end{array}

numerical-ability.question: Four pipes can fill a reservoir in 15, 20, 30 and 60 hours respectively. The first pipe was opened at 8 a.m, second at 9 a.m., third at 10 a.m. and fourth at 11 a.m. When will the reservoir be full?
numerical-ability.explanation: \begin{array}{l} Let\ the\ time\ be\ t\ hours\ after\ 8\ a.m.Then,\ the\ first\ pipe\ worked\ for\ t\ hours;\ \\ second\ pipe\ for( t\ –\ 1) \ hours;\ third\ for\ ( t\ –\ 2) \ hours\ and\ fourth\ for\ ( t\ –\ 3) \ hours.\\ \therefore \frac{t}{15} +\frac{t-1}{20} +\frac{t-2}{30} \ +\frac{t-3}{60} \ =1\ \Longrightarrow 4t+3( t-1) +2( t-2) +( t-3) =60\\ \Longrightarrow 10t=70\Longrightarrow t=7 \end{array}

numerical-ability.question: A tank is 7 metre long and 4 metre wide. At what speed should water run through a pipe 5 cm broad and 4 cm deep so that in 6 hours and 18 minutes water level in the tank rise by 4.5 metre?
numerical-ability.explanation: \begin{array}{l}Rate\ of\ flow\ of\ water\ =\ x\ cm/minute\ \therefore \ Volume\ of\ water\ that\ flowed\ in\ the\ tank\ in\ 1\ minutes=\ 5\ \times \ 4\ \times \ x\ =\ 20x\ cu.cm.\ \therefore \ Volume\ of\ water\ that\ flowed\ in\ the\ tank\ in\ 6\ hours\ 18minutes.\ i.e.\ ( 6\ \times \ 60\ +\ 18) \ =\ 378\ minutes=\ 2\ x\ \times \ 378\ cu.cm.\ According\ to\ the\ question,\ 20x\ \times \ 378\ =\ 700\ \times \ 400\ \times \ 450\ \Rightarrow x\ =\left(\frac{700*400*450*60}{10000*20*378}\right) km/hour=\ 10\ km/hour.\end{array}

verbal-reasoning.explanation: Here, afternoon sun is in the ‘west’, so if we travel ‘north’ only then our shadow would be in the ‘right’. So at the final stage he was walking towards north. But before that he made a turn left, so initially he was travelling towards east

verbal-reasoning.question: Kishenkant walks 10 km towards north. From there he walks 6 km towards south. Then he walks 3 km towards east. How far and in which direction he is with reference to his starting point?
verbal-reasoning.explanation: Kishenkant starts from O goes to A 10 km north and back to B 6 km south and finally goes to C which is 3 km east. Clearly ‘C’ is north east of ‘O’ his starting point. Now the distance is 5km NE by pythogoras theorem

verbal-reasoning.question: Bikash, pointing to his son’s picture, said to a woman. “His mother is the only daughter of your father”. How was the woman related to Bikash?
verbal-reasoning.explanation: Bikash’s son’s mother is Bikash’s wife

verbal-reasoning.question: A is father of C and D is son of B. E is brother of A. If C is sister of D, how is B related to ‘E’?
verbal-reasoning.explanation: Sister-in-law. Here, A is the father of C who is the sister of D; so, A is also the father of D who is also the son of B, so C’s mother must be B, and as E is the brother of A and B is the wife of A, so, B is the sister-in-law of E.
